reasons.rubric: Count-over-ledger predicate across possibly several banks is more complex than a boolean, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Rent screening is real, but cash and multi-account payment make the count unreliable and no bank issues it.
reasons.coherence: Predicate, issuer and disclosed data line up well.
reasons.novelty: Apartment renting is a known moment, but a payment-history predicate from a bank is a new predicate and issuer.
reasons.retention_law: Landlords have no known duty to retain full statements, so minimisation would help.
reasons.linkability: A bank-signed statistic can be presented unlinkably if the scheme is built for it.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Banks have little incentive to compute and sign such a statistic for a landlord use.
reasons.no_wallet: Landlords have scant leverage to demand a wallet proof from tenants.

reasons.rubric: Set membership is simple but frequency is low and the school's real basis is the government low-income certificate, so fit is weak.
reasons.validity: Schools rely on district-office certificates, so a Taipower roll is at best corroboration and may not suffice for the decision.
reasons.coherence: The idea undercuts itself by admitting the roll is secondary and the address may be legally required.
reasons.novelty: Close to the catalogued utility-subsidy and scholarship low-income cases, only swapping the issuer.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings are generic yes/no and attribute-only statements that the idea would read the same without.
reasons.retention_law: Unknown whether schools must keep the bill or address in the student file.
reasons.linkability: Set-membership proof can be made unlinkable and hides the address and usage.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Unknown whether Taipower would sign roll membership for third-party use.
reasons.no_wallet: Unknown whether parents have a wallet, though schools could accept paper fallback.

reasons.rubric: Uniqueness via nullifier is a simple predicate with a trusted telco issuer, but multi-line holders and the platform's wish for payment data reduce the fit to possible.
reasons.validity: Trial abuse is a real problem, but a telco credential does not guarantee one per person and platforms still want a card.
reasons.coherence: The nullifier and telco uniqueness fit, though the caveats show the uniqueness claim is not delivered.
reasons.novelty: One-person-one-account is already catalogued for brokerage, so this is a new moment on a familiar predicate.
reasons.retention_law: No evident duty to retain the phone number for trials.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telcos may not want to issue credentials, and need national-ID binding to make uniqueness hold.
reasons.no_wallet: Platforms will not add wallet friction to a signup funnel they want to be frictionless.

reasons.rubric: Non-membership in a fines list is a clean yes/no from a government source, but a transfer office already blocks the transfer and frequency is lowish, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: The need is real but the office check already protects buyers, so benefit is mostly seller privacy.
reasons.coherence: Predicate and issuer fit, but short expiry and plate-versus-person mismatch weaken the design.
reasons.novelty: Used-car transactions are untouched by the known list, with a new government issuer.
reasons.provenance: The onion-routing and confidentiality-policy borrowings are decorative metaphors; the idea reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: No known requirement for dealers to keep the full fine lookup.
reasons.linkability: A non-membership proof can be presented without linking to the issuer if built that way.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Unknown whether highway authorities would sign such a status for private use.
reasons.no_wallet: Dealers have low incentive to accept anything other than the full lookup they can do themselves.

reasons.rubric: Frequency is modest, the signal is health-related and nurses may need the disease name, so fit is weak.
reasons.validity: Return-to-school clearance is real, but outbreak management and notification duties may need the diagnosis, so a bare flag may not suffice.
reasons.coherence: The idea is consistent but its own caveat conflicts with the premise of hiding the disease.
reasons.novelty: Child health clearance for school is not touched by any known case.
reasons.retention_law: Unknown whether schools must record the disease for notifiable-disease reporting.
reasons.linkability: A validity-window flag can be unlinkable, though a small school population makes timing identifying.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals face liability and consent issues for minors and are unlikely to issue it.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents of young children and school nurses are unlikely to run a wallet flow for this.

reasons.rubric: Threshold predicate is simple, but the issuer never agreed to issue, the data is gameable, and frequency is low.
reasons.validity: A committee hire is real, but platform ratings are a weak proxy for trust and a police record is the more fitting check.
reasons.coherence: The parts fit mechanically, but the verifier's need and the proof's content are mismatched.
reasons.novelty: Courier reputation for building-management hiring is not on the known list.
reasons.retention_law: No evident duty to keep courier screenshots.
reasons.linkability: A zkTLS threshold proof discloses little else, though the platform session could be observed.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform has not agreed and its terms may forbid the proof.
reasons.no_wallet: Small management committees will not operate a zkTLS verifier.

reasons.rubric: Set membership is simple, but frequency is low and the roll is not the formal eligibility basis, so fit is weak.
reasons.validity: Schools use the district low-income certificate, so a Taipower roll would be a convenience at most and may not suffice.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit but the idea concedes the roll is not an official eligibility register.
reasons.novelty: Rewording of the catalogued utility subsidy and low-income scholarship cases, and a near duplicate of the previous idea.
reasons.retention_law: Unknown whether schools must keep a document copy for subsidy audit.
reasons.linkability: Set-membership proof can be unlinkable and hides the address and usage.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Unknown whether Taipower would sign for a use outside its own function.
reasons.no_wallet: Unknown whether parents and school offices would adopt a wallet flow.

reasons.rubric: Threshold on trips and tenure is simple, but platform-attested and secondary to official claims data, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: The need exists, but insurers price on claims and violations, so platform activity is only a supplement.
reasons.coherence: The predicate, disclosed data and issuer hang together, with a plausible privacy gain.
reasons.novelty: Gig driver tenure for lease or insurance is not on the known list.
reasons.retention_law: Insurers and lessors may be required to keep underwriting files, but a minimal proof is plausible.
reasons.linkability: A zkTLS threshold proof avoids trip-level data.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform has no stated agreement and may resist or change its pages.
reasons.no_wallet: Unknown whether fleet owners and insurers would accept a wallet-based proof.
